title: Jay Leno Checks Out the Famous Miami Vice “Daytona”

body_markdown: Some of the most famous cars were driven by famous actors, but what happens when the car is doing a little acting as well? For the show *Miami Vice* , the cast included not just the people but also the cars, and when you need the perfect car to behave perfectly in every scene, you need essentially the perfect film car: one that is easy to fix, easy to drive, and looks exactly right from every angle. That’s easier said than done. Exhibit A is one of the star cars from *Miami Vice* . This week Jay Leno[gets up close and personal](https://youtu.be/qjkP-ORfEZY?si=BB8xDzKhCKOkOhm6) with a Corvette that slipped into an Italian suit—and with the tailor who created the suit and went on to sell many more like it, though that put him in hot water. The[saga of McBurnie Coachcraft](https://www.hagerty.com/media/entertainment/the-miami-vice-california-daytona-spyder-the-tv-car-enzo-ferrari-despised/) and the star car of *Miami Vice* actually started with a different business venture, born when businessman Al Mardikian approached coachbuilder Tom McBurnie about fabricating and producing the body for a Cobra kit car. The idea didn’t pan out financially, but before Mardikian could leave, McBurnie pitched the idea of a Daytona kit instead. One could say the rest is history, but they would be wrong, as the most interesting bits of the story were yet to come. Jay Leno's Garage Jay Leno's Garage Jay Leno's Garage Replicating a car can sometimes be more difficult than creating something from scratch, since there are expectations for what a replica should look like. McBurnie used a 1976 Corvette as the base. The difference in wheelbase between the Vette and the real Daytona was just over 4.5, but otherwise the two were pretty close dimensionally. McBurnie drew up a design, started molding, and then finally began bonding fiberglass parts to the Corvette, and after nearly a year the first car took shape. That car plus three others were delivered to Al Mardikian, who started the whole adventure. To celebrate these beautiful new creations, Mardikian hosted a party whose star-studded guest list included people connected to Universal Studios. Though the pre-production of *Miami Vice* was already underway, the star cars had not yet been decided. In short order, two of McBurnie’s creations were leased for production. That’s the fun part of the story, and the rest of the tale involving the transformation of McBurnie Coachcraft from a two-person shop to one with 55 employees turning out 92 cars and more than 300 kits is best told by the man himself in the video above. It almost reads like the storyline of a TV drama.
